payload.detail: CARRIED FORWARD 2026-09-06 from #A3AHCX, closed the same day as a duplicate of this row. That row (2026-08-24) held technical detail this one did not, preserved here so the merge loses nothing: validateGovernedMessage lives in src/lib/caring-contacts/message-policy.ts and enforces the segment limit, the prohibited vocabulary, the required support fragments and, from 2026-08-24, the fictional-contact check. When a dispatch or preview path is built, wiring it to this validator is the first requirement. Recorded so nobody mistakes 'the validator refuses this' for 'the system refuses this'. PROCESS NOTE: this defect was recorded twice, eleven days apart, by two sessions that did not find each other's row, and graded P2 the first time and P1 the second. It is the clearest evidence for the ledger's missing dedupe-on-intake step. CORRECTED AND GUARDED 2026-09-07, verified against main at fe8db888d. Two claims carried forward above are now out of date and are struck here rather than left to mislead a later reader - which is precisely the failure mode this row itself documents. (1) 'A grep across src/ and worker/ finds no production caller; it is exercised only by tests' is FALSE as of 2026-09-02. resolveClosingContactMessageBody at message-policy.ts:320 calls validateGovernedMessage in production code. It arrived with #59JT7W, which deliberately moved the unauthored-body rule INTO the chokepoint so that a sender obtaining a body by some other route could not meet no refusal at all. (2) The domain does carry dispatch scaffolding this row does not mention: DispatchRecord, dispatchKey and sendableContacts all exist. THE ROW STAYS OPEN AND P1 BECAUSE THE SUBSTANTIVE POINT HOLDS. No message body exists anywhere in the domain for a sender to send. PlannedContact (schedule.ts:23) names a messageType but holds no text, and DispatchRecord (repository.ts:730) tracks attempt number and provider status but no content. Nothing outbound is gated because nothing is outbound. The validator is the mechanism a future sender must use, not a control that is currently failing open. NOW GUARDED: tests/caring-contacts-message-body-chokepoint.test.ts, merged in PR #2690, pins both shapes as bodyless with exact-key type assertions. A message body can only reach a recipient by first riding one of those two shapes, so adding a body field to either is the exact moment the wiring becomes required, and it now fails typecheck naming the offending field instead of passing silently. Verified by mutation rather than by a green run: adding 'body?: string' to PlannedContact produces TS2322, 'Type boolean is not assignable to type { unexpectedOnActual: "body" }'. NEXT ACTION unchanged: when a dispatch or preview path is built, route its body through validateGovernedMessage before anything can send it, and widen the pinned key lists only as part of that same change.
